topics.title: Project: Shaking Button
topics.summary: A button that shakes with a keyframe animation when hovered.
topics.description:
**Goal**: a call-to-action button that wiggles on hover to attract attention.

### Concepts used
- Basic button styling (`padding`, `border`, `background: transparent`).
- A **pseudo-class** (`:hover`) to trigger the effect.
- A short **@keyframes** animation using the individual `rotate` property.
- `animation-iteration-count` - the shake runs once per hover.

### How it works
1. Style the button with a purple border and text.
2. On `:hover`, change the color and attach `animation: shaking .2s linear`.
3. The keyframes rotate the element to `20deg`, `-20deg` and back to `20deg`. Because the animation is short and plays once, it looks like a quick shake.

### Improvements you can try
- Use `animation-iteration-count: 2` for a stronger shake.
- Use `translateX` instead of `rotate` for a horizontal "no" shake.
- Wrap the hover animation in `@media (hover: hover)` and `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Add `transform-origin: bottom center` to make it swing like a bell.

### Why not transition?
A transition only goes from A to B. A shake needs several back-and-forth steps, so keyframes are the right tool.
keyPoints: Keyframes create multi-step motion that transitions cannot
rotate / translate are cheap, compositor friendly properties
Trigger with :hover; the animation runs once per hover
Short durations (0.2-0.5s) feel like a shake
Respect reduced-motion preferences
pitfalls: Animating on hover only, so touch users never see it
Long infinite shaking that distracts and hurts accessibility

examples.title: Shake me

interview.q: How would you make a button shake on hover?
interview.a: Define @keyframes alternating rotate or translateX values and apply animation: shaking .2s linear on :hover.

interview.q: Why use keyframes instead of a transition here?
interview.a: A transition only interpolates between two states; a shake needs multiple back-and-forth steps.

topics.title: Project: Neon Circle Loader
topics.summary: A glowing rotating ring loader made with ::before, ::after and stacked box-shadows.
topics.description:
**Goal**: a neon spinner using a single HTML element.

### Concepts used
- **aspect-ratio** and **border-radius: 50%** to create circles.
- **::before** to cut a hole in the middle (a dark circle on top of a purple circle).
- **::after** for the glowing "head" using multiple `box-shadow` layers.
- **position: relative/absolute** to place pseudo-elements.
- **@keyframes** with `rotate: 360deg` and `animation-direction: reverse`.

### Step by step
1. `.loader` is a purple circle that rotates infinitely and linearly.
2. `::before` is a slightly smaller circle painted with the page background color. It looks like the loader is a ring.
3. `::after` is a small circle at the top of the ring with five growing shadows, producing the neon glow.
4. Since the whole element rotates, the glowing dot travels around the ring.

### Tips
- Use `currentColor` or a custom property for the neon color to theme it easily.
- Keep the ::before color equal to the surface behind the loader. For a transparent ring use a border + conic-gradient + mask instead.
- Use `animation-timing-function: linear` for continuous spinners.
keyPoints: One element + two pseudo-elements build the whole loader
Layered box-shadow creates the neon glow
Rotate the parent so children move along the ring
linear + infinite is right for spinners
Use a custom property to recolor the glow
pitfalls: Inner circle color not matching the background (ring looks wrong)
Forgetting content: "" on pseudo-elements

examples.title: Neon loader

interview.q: How do you create a glow effect in CSS?
interview.a: Stack several box-shadows (or text-shadows) of the same color with increasing blur radii.

interview.q: How is the ring made from one element?
interview.a: The element is a filled circle; ::before places a smaller circle in the background color on top, leaving a ring visible.

topics.title: Project: Newton's Cradle
topics.summary: Pendulum balls swinging with transform-origin, nth-child selectors and delayed keyframes.
topics.description:
**Goal**: recreate the desk toy where the outer balls swing alternately. ### Concepts used - **Flexbox** (`display: flex; justify-content: center; gap`) to place five strings. - **::before** as the ball at the end of each string. - **:first-child / :last-child** to animate only the two outer balls. - **transform-origin: top** so a string pivots from its top end. - **@keyframes** + **animation-delay** so the right ball swings when the left one stops. ### Structure ```html
``` Each `div` is a thin vertical string; its `::before` is the ball placed near the bottom (`top: 90%`). ### Timing Both animations last 2s. The left one swings from 0 to 30deg at 25%, back at 50%, and rests until 100%. The right one uses the same time but starts with a **1s delay**, so the swings alternate. ### Make it better - Add a frame (top bar) using a border-top on the container (as in the source). - Use `ease-out` going up and `ease-in` coming down for more realistic motion. - Use custom properties for string length and ball size.
keyPoints: transform-origin sets the pivot at the top of the string
:first-child and :last-child target the outer balls
animation-delay offsets the two swings by half a cycle
Pseudo-elements draw the balls (no extra HTML)
Keyframes rest at 0deg for the second half to make a pause
pitfalls: Pivoting around the center (default origin) makes the string rotate in place
Using margin hacks for ball position instead of the string length

examples.title: Newton's cradle

interview.q: Why is transform-origin important in a pendulum animation?
interview.a: The default origin is the center, which would spin the string around its middle; setting it to the top makes it swing from the pivot point.

interview.q: How do you offset two animations that use the same keyframes?
interview.a: Give one of them an animation-delay (e.g. half of the duration).

topics.summary: Two text effects: a typewriter-like reveal using ::before and a swaying floating heading.
keyPoints: ::before duplicates text with content: "..."
overflow: hidden + animated width reveals text
alternate direction makes back-and-forth motion
text-shadow adds depth to floating text
clip-path is a lighter alternative to width animation
pitfalls: Duplicated text in content is not accessible - keep the real text in HTML
Width animation on long paragraphs causes layout work

examples.title: Text reveal
Floating text

interview.q: How can you create a typewriter-like reveal effect?
interview.a: Overlay text using ::before, hide overflow, and animate its width (or clip-path) from 0 to 100% with a caret border.

interview.q: Why is width animation not ideal for performance?
interview.a: It changes layout every frame; clip-path or transform animations avoid layout and are cheaper.

topics.title: Project: Falling Rain Background
topics.summary: Create a rain effect by sliding a repeating background pattern with background-position.
topics.description:
**Goal**: an endless rain overlay on top of a dark sky.

### The trick
Instead of animating hundreds of elements, **animate the background position** of one element that has a repeating raindrop pattern. The pattern tile repeats, so moving it diagonally looks like falling rain.

In the source course the pattern came from a PNG (`rain.png`). Here we make the tile with gradients so no image is needed.

### Steps
1. Give the container a dark gradient background (the sky).
2. Add an overlay element with a **tile pattern**: several thin diagonal lines drawn with `linear-gradient` and `background-size`.
3. Animate `background-position` from `0 0` to the tile size (so the loop is seamless).
4. Use a short duration (0.4-0.8s) with `linear` and `infinite`.

### Concepts used
- Multiple backgrounds and gradient patterns.
- `background-size` for tiles, `background-position` for motion.
- `@keyframes` with seamless loops: end position = tile size.

### Improvements
- Add two overlay layers with different speeds and sizes for depth (parallax rain).
- Add a flash with an animated `opacity` for lightning.
- Reduce opacity or disable under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
keyPoints: Move a repeating background instead of many elements
Tile size = animation distance for a seamless loop
Gradients can draw thin lines/patterns
Layer two speeds for depth
linear + infinite for continuous motion
pitfalls: Animation jumping because the end position is not a multiple of the tile size
Full-screen animated backgrounds hurting low-end devices

examples.title: Rain overlay
examples.html: Cozy rainy day

interview.q: How would you build a rain effect efficiently?
interview.a: Use one element with a repeating pattern background and animate background-position by exactly one tile; avoid animating hundreds of DOM nodes.

interview.q: Why must the animation end position equal the tile size?
interview.a: So the last frame looks identical to the first, producing a seamless infinite loop.

topics.title: Project: Sun, Moon and Changing Sky
topics.summary: An eclipse-like scene: a sky that changes color and a moon sliding across the sun.
topics.description:
**Goal**: a square "universe" whose sky color cycles through day and night while a dark moon passes in front of the sun.

### Concepts used
- **aspect-ratio: 1** and viewport units for responsive squares.
- **Flexbox centering** for the sun in the middle.
- **overflow: hidden** + **border-radius** so the moon is clipped to the circular sun.
- **::after** as the moon; **translate** and **scale** animated with keyframes.
- **Two independent animations** on different elements (sky and moon) with the same duration.

### How it works
1. The sky (`.universe`) animates `background-color` between warm orange and black (0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%).
2. The sun is a circle with `position: relative; overflow: hidden`.
3. `.sun::after` is a black circle the same size. It starts off to the right (`translate: 100%`), passes over the sun (`translate: 0`) and leaves to the left (`-100%`).
4. At the midpoint the moon covers the sun (total eclipse) and gets a soft white glow via `box-shadow`.

### Notes
- The source code used native CSS nesting (`&::after`) inside `.sun`.
- Because both animations share a duration (8s) and are infinite, they stay in sync.
- Use the individual `translate`/`scale` properties for clean keyframes.
keyPoints: overflow: hidden clips the moon inside the sun circle
Two animations with the same duration stay in sync
aspect-ratio keeps the elements square
translate and scale individual properties simplify keyframes
Nesting (&::after) keeps related rules together
pitfalls: Forgetting position: relative on the sun, so the moon positions against another ancestor
Using px sizes that break on small screens (use % or vw)

examples.title: Eclipse scene

interview.q: How does the moon stay inside the sun circle?
interview.a: The sun has overflow: hidden and border-radius: 50%, so anything that moves outside its circle is clipped.
It adds a decorative element without extra HTML and can be positioned absolutely inside the relatively positioned sun.

topics.title: Project: Parallax Sections
topics.summary: Full-width sections with fixed backgrounds and gradient overlays for a parallax scroll.
topics.description:
**Goal**: sections whose background stays still while the content scrolls over it. ### Concepts used - **background-attachment: fixed** - the background is attached to the viewport, not the element. - **Layered backgrounds**: a semi-transparent overlay gradient above the image makes white text readable. - **Grid centering**: `display: grid; place-items: center;`. - **text-shadow** for legibility. ### Structure ```html

Parallax

...

...
...
``` ### CSS idea ```css section { min-height: 100vh; display: grid; place-items: center; text-align: center; background-image: linear-gradient(rgba(0,0,0,.3), rgba(0,0,0,.3)), url(photo.jpg); background-size: cover; background-attachment: fixed; /* the parallax part */ } .section-2 { background-attachment: scroll; } /* alternate for contrast */ ``` Alternating `fixed` and `scroll` sections creates the "reveal" feeling of the original demo. ### Caveats - iOS Safari ignores `fixed` on most versions; use a fallback (`scroll`) via `@supports` or a media query for touch devices. - Large fixed backgrounds force repaints while scrolling; keep images compressed. - For real depth, use 3D transforms with `perspective` on the scroller.
keyPoints: background-attachment: fixed pins the background to the viewport
Overlay gradient improves text contrast
Alternate fixed and scroll sections for the effect
Fixed backgrounds are poorly supported on iOS
Use compressed images and a reduced-effect fallback
pitfalls: Text unreadable without an overlay
Relying on fixed attachment on mobile
Combining background-attachment: fixed with transforms on ancestors (breaks)

interview.q: How do you make a simple parallax effect with CSS?
interview.a: Use background-attachment: fixed with a background-image so the image stays in place while the section scrolls.

interview.q: What problem exists with background-attachment: fixed on mobile?
interview.a: Many mobile browsers (especially iOS Safari) do not support it properly, so provide a scroll fallback.

topics.title: Project: Auto Image Slideshow
topics.summary: A pure-CSS crossfade slideshow using stacked layers and staggered keyframes.
topics.description: **Goal**: a gallery that automatically changes slides forever with no JavaScript. ### The source approach The original demo animated `background-image` inside `@keyframes` (0%, 20%, 40%...) over 20s. It works, but background images **cannot be interpolated**, so slides switch abruptly without fading, and all images are requested via CSS. ### A smoother approach: stacked layers 1. Stack N slides with `position: absolute; inset: 0;`. 2. Give every slide the **same** animation (fade in, hold, fade out) with `opacity`. 3. Offset each slide with `animation-delay` equal to `duration / N`. For 4 slides and a 12s cycle: delays of 0s, 3s, 6s, 9s. Each slide is visible for ~25% of the cycle. ### Keyframes ```css @keyframes slide { 0%, 25% { opacity: 1; } /* visible */ 33%, 92% { opacity: 0; } /* hidden */ 100% { opacity: 1; } } ``` (Adjust percentages so fades overlap slightly.) ### Notes - Use real `` elements with `object-fit: cover` for content images (alt text and lazy loading). - Pause on hover: `.carousel:hover .slide { animation-play-state: paused; }` - For user-controlled sliders use scroll-snap (see Modern CSS). - Add `prefers-reduced-motion` to stop the autoplay.
keyPoints: background-image cannot be smoothly animated
Stack slides and animate opacity with staggered delays
delay = cycle duration / number of slides
Pause on hover with animation-play-state
Add reduced-motion handling for autoplay
pitfalls: Autoplay with no way to pause (accessibility)
Loading all images eagerly at large sizes
Percent keyframes that never fully hide the previous slide (ghosting)

examples.html:

interview.q: Why is animating background-image between photos not smooth?
interview.a: Images are not interpolable values, so the property switches at keyframes; stacking elements and animating opacity creates a real crossfade.

interview.q: How do you offset each slide in a CSS slideshow?
interview.a: Use the same animation on all slides with animation-delay increments of cycle-duration / number-of-slides.

topics.title: Project: Responsive Landing Page
topics.summary: Combine variables, grid, flexbox, nesting and media queries into a complete responsive page.
topics.description:
The final project of the course is a multipage responsive website. Here is its **core architecture** reduced to one page.

### What it uses
| Feature | Where |
|---|---|
| Reset | `* { margin: 0; padding: 0; box-sizing: border-box; }` |
| Theme tokens | `:root { --main-color; --heading-color; --para-color; ... }` |
| rem-based sizing | `html { font-size: 62.5% }` -> `1rem = 10px` |
| Layout helpers | `.container`, `.grid`, `.grid-two--cols`, `.grid-three--cols` |
| Reusable modules | `.btn`, `.section-common-heading` |
| Nesting | `& a::after { ... }` for animated nav underline |
| Responsive steps | `@media (width <= 998px)` switches 2 columns to 1 and reorders with `order` |
| Polished details | `:is()` to group sections, `:nth-child()` for icon colors, transitions on hover |

### Page structure
1. **Header**: logo + navigation (`flex`, `space-between`).
2. **Hero**: two-column grid (text + visual) that stacks on mobile.
3. **Features**: grid of cards `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(...))`.
4. **Call-to-action** and **footer**.

### Build order (recommended)
1. HTML structure with semantic tags.
2. Tokens + reset + typography.
3. Layout helpers.
4. Components (button, card).
5. Section styles.
6. Media queries (mobile-first or adjust down).
7. Test with DevTools device toolbar.

### Skills practised
Everything from the previous sections: box model, selectors, flex, grid, transitions and responsive design.
keyPoints: Tokens in :root keep the theme consistent
Container + grid helpers speed up layout
Stack columns and reorder with media queries
Hover transitions and nested pseudo-elements add polish
Build in layers: reset, tokens, layout, components, sections
pitfalls: Starting with pixel-perfect desktop only and fixing mobile at the end
Duplicating styles instead of building reusable modules

interview.q: How do you structure CSS for a multi-page website?
interview.a: Start with a reset and tokens, then layout helpers (container/grid), reusable components (button, heading), section styles, and finally responsive media queries; reuse one stylesheet across pages.

interview.q: How do you reorder content on mobile without changing HTML?
interview.a: Use flex/grid order or place items in a different grid-template-areas inside a media query (mind accessibility of visual vs DOM order).
